events.description: MBC correspondent met Bin-Ladin, Zawahiri and Abu-Hafs in the Qandahar desert; footage of training and maneuvers provided by al-Qa'idah media office.
MBC broadcast the video report; Taliban Foreign Minister statement that Afghan territory will not be used for attacks.
MBC correspondent Bakr Atyani meets Bin-Ladin, Zawahiri and Abu-Hafs at Bin-Ladin's headquarters in the Qandahar desert, after a three-hour drive in a car with darkened windows and searches.
MBC broadcasts video report showing Bin-Ladin's followers in military training and preparing strikes against US and Israeli interests.
Taleban Foreign Minister Mutawakkil says the Islamic Emirate will not allow its territory to be used to strike other countries or for terrorism.
Abu-Hafs says Al-Qa'idah is ready to vacate positions in under half an hour if the US bombs them.
Egyptian Al-Jama'ah al-Islamiyah recently joined Bin-Ladin's group, forming the Al-Qa'idah Organization as then known.

key_claims: Al-Qa'idah conducts continuous military maneuvers and training in the Afghan desert in preparation for strikes on US interests.
Egyptian Al-Jama'ah al-Islamiyah under Zawahiri is said to have joined Bin-Ladin's group to form al-Qa'idah.
Abu-Hafs is Bin-Ladin's right-hand man and says al-Qa'idah can vacate positions in under half an hour.
The Taleban ban Bin-Ladin from press statements while publicly denying terrorist use of Afghan territory.
